conventions.convention: The horizon τ is finite and positive, and the covariate dimension p is a fixed positive integer. Vector predictability means coordinatewise predictability in one stated filtration.
U=min(T,C), δ=1{T≤C}, Y(t)=1{U≥t}, and R(t) includes subjects whose observation endpoint equals t. Predictability of Y is required separately.

The baseline hazard density is nonnegative, measurable and integrable; its cumulative hazard is absolutely continuous. Conditional independence of event and censoring times given the covariate-history sigma-algebra is an explicit model assumption.

The untied partial likelihood has empty product 1. Grouped-time subset and coarsened-order tie contributions have distinct explicit conditional-law assumptions. A hazard quotient is asserted only where the baseline hazard is positive.
Risk sums use Z⊗0=1, Z⊗1=Z and Z⊗2=ZZᵀ. Sample weighted means and covariance matrices are set to zero when their denominator is zero. Population risk support has inf over t≤τ of s⁽⁰⁾(t,β₀)>0.

Integrated parameter-uniform convergence requires bounded predictable IID records; uniform convergence in time additionally requires pointwise measurability and finite L¹(P) bracketing numbers at every positive width.

Stochastic integrals are L² completions, with vector and matrix integrals interpreted coordinatewise. Their pathwise identification holds almost surely at each fixed terminal time, without assuming left continuity of the bounded predictable integrand.

Inference assumes AC, square-integrable counting-process martingale contracts in a common filtration, no tied failures, positive definite I, and a measurable consistent estimator solving the score equation with probability tending to one. Existence or consistency of such a root is not concluded.

load_bearing.statement: For IID jointly measurable predictable subject records with uniformly bounded covariates, compact B containing β₀ and positive population risk support, the parameter-uniform risk-sum errors converge in expected squared error at each fixed time and integrated against every finite deterministic measure ν(dt)=w(t)dt with nonnegative integrable w. Sample denominators have a uniform positive lower bound on events of probability tending to one; weighted-mean and covariance errors have the corresponding fixed-time and integrated convergence. Uniform-in-time convergence additionally assumes pointwise-measurable coordinate classes with finite L¹(P) bracketing numbers at every positive width.

Under the counting-process contract, E∫G dN=E∫G dA for every nonnegative predictable G. For every bounded real predictable H, the L²-completed integral equals Σ HₜΔNₜ−∫H dA almost surely at every fixed terminal time, also coordinatewise for vector or matrix integrands.

Under the stated IID bounded-covariate model, risk-support hypotheses, no-tie event process and per-subject counting-process contracts, n⁻¹ᐟ²Uₙ(β₀)=n⁻¹ᐟ²Σᵢξᵢ+o_P(1), where ξᵢ=∫(Zᵢ−z̄)dMᵢ are IID centered square-integrable vectors with covariance I. Their normalized sum is O_P(1).

Under the risk-set lemma's IID bounded-covariate, risk-support and compact-set hypotheses, per-subject counting-process contracts on one common filtration and no simultaneous failures, sup over β∈B of ‖n⁻¹Hₙ(β)+J(β)‖max tends to zero in probability. J is continuous and J(β₀)=I.

Under its stated AC, IID Cox model, bounded predictability, positive risk support, common-filtration martingale contracts, no-tie and positive-definite-information hypotheses, every measurable consistent score root satisfies √n(β̂ₙ−β₀)=I⁻¹n⁻¹ᐟ²Σᵢ∫(Zᵢ−z̄)dMᵢ+o_P(1).

Specifies the conditional event intensity Yᵢ(t)λ₀(t)exp(β₀ᵀZᵢ(t)), right-censoring and predictable-risk conventions, the untied risk-set partial likelihood, and separately qualified tie conventions. The counting-process martingale property is a separate model-contract assumption.

concerns.concern: Proof 4.1 ends: “No such time-indexed class hypothesis was used in steps 1.1–4.1.” Step 4.1 itself explicitly assumes [A1] and applies its pointwise-measurability and bracketing conditions. The sentence should delimit the earlier integrated-convergence argument; its present endpoint incorrectly includes the conditional branch. The statements and preceding derivations remain sound.

seams_checked.note: The supplier and Cox definition agree on U=min(T,C), δ=1{T≤C}, including event/censoring ties. Cox explicitly assumes conditional independence given covariate history and does not infer martingale or empirical adequacy claims from the observation supplier.

The consumers retain the supplier's simple-count, continuous-compensator, square-integrable-martingale and finite-energy requirements. No simultaneous failures makes the aggregate count simple; bounded covariates and integrable baseline supply its energy bounds. The pathwise-identity lemma supplies the additional identification needed for arbitrary bounded predictable integrands.

The Cox corollary applies the terminal theorem only after obtaining a measurable one-subject influence function, centered finite-second-moment contributions and the estimator expansion. It does not use the terminal theorem to justify random-risk-mean replacement, consistency or a process-level limit.
